purpose: Stature-conditioned global landmark scaffold for the skeleton-first canonical adult male. These are anthropometric landmark corridors, not whole-bone lengths.
rules: Use bony anthropometric landmarks directly only when the ANSUR definition matches the canonical landmark.
Surface landmarks are diagnostics unless an explicit bone/skin offset is defined.
Residual SD is a population corridor, not an optimization target.
Bone-specific morphometry and joint-centre evidence override a surface landmark if definitions conflict.

trochanterion_height.use: pelvis/femur scaffold; HJC kept ~8 mm below only as the separate radiographic relation already recorded

wrist_height.use: distal upper-limb global check, not a direct radius endpoint without landmark mapping

biacromial_breadth.current_r95_measurement_warning: a003 report used a surface corner as the character comparator; canonical target must use actual acromial bony landmarks.

acromion_to_fingertip.use: global chain check after radius/hand retarget

high_value_implications: At 1.82 m, ANSUR-conditioned biacromial breadth is ~425 mm with residual SD ~16 mm. This provides a stature-aware global skeletal shoulder-width scaffold independent of the oversized r95 shoulder surface.
Acromial height is already close to population expectation, so shoulder correction should primarily change lateral girdle geometry rather than arbitrarily lowering the entire shoulder.
Knee/tibial/malleolar landmark heights are already close to the current fit, reinforcing provisional retention of the lower-limb vertical chain.
Wrist/arm-chain targets remain useful global checks but do not define radius/ulna bone endpoints by themselves.
